issues.body: `_normalize_path_entry` strips `./` but does not canonicalize internal `.` or `..` segments. An upload path such as `target/../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json` resolves at runtime to the workspace-root divergence log, while `_glob_to_re` compares the unnormalized text to the relative target and returns false. The existing traversal-looking fixture contains `${{ matrix.shard }}`, so it is rejected only as dynamic and does not exercise this static bypass. A future broad or exact upload using a statically resolvable parent segment could therefore retain the file while the promised regression test stays green.
issues.fix_hint: Normalize static path entries lexically against a synthetic workspace root before glob matching, rejecting any path that escapes that root; preserve glob metacharacters while resolving only `.` and `..` path segments. Add positive fixtures for `target/../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json`, `foo/./../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json`, and a directory form that normalizes to the workspace root, plus an escaping-path fixture handled conservatively.
issues.title: Static parent-directory paths bypass the artifact matcher

verdict.summary: Round 3 fixes the prior expression-based and absolute-workspace-path bypasses, but the artifact-retention matcher still compares non-dynamic paths without resolving dot segments. GitHub Actions resolves upload paths against the workspace, so a static path containing `..` can name the divergence log while this test reports that it cannot. Because this is a new bypass of the load-bearing regression check, progress is regressing.
